source_spans.locator: Nature Reviews Neuroscience 11 (2010), published p.114, Abstract: the earlier synchronized sleep phase supports reactivation/redistribution, whereas the later desynchronized phase might favour subsequent local stabilization

Nature Reviews Neuroscience 11 (2010), published pp.117-118, synaptic-consolidation discussion and Box 2: fast-learning temporary versus slower-learning long-term stores, parallel initial encoding, and reactivation-driven gradual redistribution

Nature Reviews Neuroscience 11 (2010), published pp.121-122, active system-consolidation and later-stage local-plasticity sections: repeated reactivation strengthens long-term cortical representations; later-stage linkage remains explicitly tentative

Nature Reviews Neuroscience 11 (2010), published p.123, Figure 3 and Conclusions: complementary sequential contributions of the two phases; ensuing desynchronized sleep might stabilize representations reorganized earlier, with direct evidence stated to be scarce

conditions: post-learning sleep containing an earlier synchronized phase followed by an ensuing desynchronized phase
temporal_scope: new events are encoded during waking before post-learning consolidation
an earlier synchronized sleep phase precedes an ensuing desynchronized phase in the proposed sequence
the two-stage model distinguishes a fast-learning temporary store from a slower-learning long-term store

nodes.description: newly acquired representation initially encoded in parallel in a fast-learning temporary store and a slower-learning long-term store
fast-learning intermediate store that retains newly encoded information temporarily and is represented by the hippocampus for declarative memories
slower-learning long-term store whose corresponding representation is gradually strengthened and integrated and is represented by neocortical networks for declarative memories
earlier post-learning phase characterized by widespread synchronized activity and repeated reactivation
proposed redistribution and integration driven by repeated reactivation of the fast-store trace and concurrent reactivation of the corresponding slow-store trace
ensuing post-learning phase characterized by more desynchronized and locally disentangled activity
proposed local strengthening and stabilization of cortical representations that underwent reorganization during the earlier phase

relations.description: the earlier synchronized phase precedes the ensuing desynchronized phase in the proposed normal sequence
new events are initially encoded in parallel in the fast-learning temporary store and the slower-learning long-term store

during the earlier phase, repeated reactivation of the temporary-store trace is proposed to drive concurrent reactivation and gradual strengthening and integration of the corresponding long-term-store representation
the ensuing phase is proposed to support local stabilization of representations reorganized during the earlier phase; the source states that direct evidence for this stage linkage is scarce
